# Consolidated TEXT: 31992L0058 — EN — 26.07.2019

CELEX 01992L0058-20190726 · EN · 11/17 · konsolidacja dokumentacyjna · [źródło](https://publications.europa.eu/resource/cellar/08dbd0a1-e080-11e9-9c4e-01aa75ed71a1.0001.03/DOC_1)

<a id="anx_III"></a>

<a id="id-82f594b5-a366-462f-a39c-aa9c52698629"></a>ANNEX III

<a id="id-6aa04774-f064-4240-ae93-ea8cc2451705"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS GOVERNING SIGNS ON CONTAINERS AND PIPES

<a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32014L0027" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="32014L0027: REPLACED">▼M2</a>

1.&nbsp;Containers used at work for chemical substances or mixtures classified as hazardous according to the criteria for any physical or health hazard class in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, and containers used for the storage of such hazardous substances or mixtures, together with the visible pipes containing or transporting such hazardous substances and mixtures, must be labelled with the relevant hazard pictograms in accordance with that Regulation.

The first paragraph does not apply to containers used at work for brief periods nor to containers whose contents change frequently, provided that alternative adequate measures are taken, in particular for information and/or training, which guarantee the same level of protection.

The labels referred to in the first paragraph may be:

—

replaced by warning signs set out in Annex II, using the same pictograms or symbols. If there is no equivalent warning sign in Section 3.2 of Annex II, the relevant hazard pictogram set out in Annex V of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 must be used,

—

supplemented by additional information, such as the name and/or formula of the hazardous substance or mixture and the details of the hazard,

—

for the transporting of containers at the place of work, supplemented or replaced by signs that are applicable throughout the Union for the transport of hazardous substances or mixtures.

<a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/31992L0058" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="31992L0058">▼B</a>

2.&nbsp;Signs must be mounted as follows:

—

on the visible side(s),

—

in unpliable, self-adhesive or painted form.

3.&nbsp;Where appropriate, the signs referred to in section 1 of this Annex must have the intrinsic features defined in section 1.4. of Annex II and must fulfill the conditions of use for signboards laid down in section 2 of Annex II.

4.&nbsp;Without prejudice to sections 1,2 and 3, the labels used on pipes must be positioned visibly in the vicinity of the most dangerous points, such as valves and joint, and at reasonable intervals.

5.&nbsp;Areas, rooms or enclosures used for the storage of significant quantities of
                     <a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32014L0027" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="32014L0027: REPLACED">
                        <span class="boldface">►M2</span>
                     </a>
                  &nbsp;hazardous&nbsp;◄  substances or
                     <a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32014L0027" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="32014L0027: REPLACED">
                        <span class="boldface">►M2</span>
                     </a>
                  &nbsp;mixtures&nbsp;◄  must be indicated by a suitable warning sign taken from section 3.2 of Annex II, or marked as provided in section 1 of Annex III, unless the labelling of the individual packages or containers is adequate for this purpose, taking into account Annex II, point 1.5 with regard to dimensions.

Stores of a number of
                  <a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32014L0027" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="32014L0027: REPLACED">
                     <span class="boldface">►M2</span>
                  </a>
               &nbsp;hazardous&nbsp;◄  substances or
                  <a href="http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32014L0027" onclick="window.open(this.href,'_blank'); return false;" title="32014L0027: REPLACED">
                     <span class="boldface">►M2</span>
                  </a>
               &nbsp;mixtures&nbsp;◄  may be indicated by the warning sign for general danger.

The signs or labels referred to above must be positioned, as appropriate, near the storage area or on the door leading into the storage room.

<a id="anx_IV"></a>

<a id="id-edefae0a-ed23-4b1a-82a8-73c3adc3be18"></a>ANNEX IV

<a id="id-11e8387c-9aa9-411c-8d41-64d566d5638b"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR THE IDENTIFICATION AND LOCATION OF FIRE-FIGHTING EQUIPMENT

<a id="id-ace2cf95-f35c-49dc-a35f-5e54ef199d52"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Preliminary remark

This Annex applies to equipment used exclusively for fire-fighting purposes.

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">Fire-fighting equipment must be identified by using a specific colour for the equipment and placing a location signboard, and/or by using a specific colour for the places where such equipment is kept, or their access points.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">3.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The colour for identifying this equipment is red.</p>
<p class="norm">The red area must be sufficiently large to allow the equipment to be identified easily.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">4.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The signboards provided for in section 3.5 of Annex Ii must be used to mark the locations of this equipment.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<a id="anx_V"></a>

<a id="id-d5165838-c6ea-4664-9d10-316babf71b28"></a>ANNEX V

<a id="id-c3707a1b-a9a3-4246-a4cd-8e3b56877144"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS GOVERNING SIGNS USED FOR OBSTACLES AND DANGEROUS LOCATIONS, AND FOR MARKING TRAFFIC ROUTES

<a id="id-f5975c08-e730-4a7e-94c2-328e040fa860"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Signs for obstacles and dangerous locations

1.1.&nbsp;Places where there is a risk of colliding with obstacles, of falling or of objects falling should be marked with alternating yellow and black, or red and white stripes in built-up zones in the undertaking to which workers have access during their work.

1.2.&nbsp;The dimensions of the markings must be commensurate with the scale of the obstacle or dangerous location in question.

1.3.&nbsp;The yellow and black or red and white stripes must be at an angle of approximately 45&nbsp;° and of more or less equal size.

1.4.&nbsp;Example:

<img src="data:image/jpg;base64," width="276" height="51" alt="image">

<a id="id-8a1417fa-146a-4649-b4d0-479d61d7235a"></a>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Marking of traffic routes

2.1.&nbsp;Where the use and equipment of rooms so requires for the protection of workers, traffic routes for vehicles must be clearly identified by continous stripes in a clearly visible colour, preferably white or yellow, taking into account the colour of the ground.

2.2.&nbsp;The stripes must be located so as to indicate the necessary safe distance between the vehicles and any object which may be near by, and between pedestrians and vehicles.

2.3.&nbsp;Permanent traffic routes in built-up areas outdoors should, as far as is practicable, be similarly marked, unless they are provided with suitable barriers or pavements.

<a id="anx_VI"></a>

<a id="id-5616638a-a981-4539-9187-a87c8e43dfe3"></a>ANNEX VI

<a id="id-dbe39133-383c-4324-9f30-ffffb8c8b806"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR ILLUMINATED SIGNS

<a id="id-75cd7bc4-9628-4367-bbfa-dc70ec417c28"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intrinsic features

1.1.&nbsp;The light emitted by a sign must produce a luminous contrast which is appropriate to its environment, in accordance with the intended conditions of use of the sign, but without producing glare for an excessive amount of light or poor visibility as a result of insufficient light.

1.2.&nbsp;The luminous area emitting a sign may be of a single colour or contain a pictogram on a specified background.

1.3.&nbsp;The single colour must correspond to the table of colours and their meanings set out in section 4 of Annex I.

1.4.&nbsp;Likewise, when the sign contains a pictogram, the latter must comply with all the relevant rules set out in Annex II.

<a id="id-accdb8d5-8fc6-4982-8e41-1ecbba2bc83e"></a>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Specific rules governing use

2.1.&nbsp;If a device can emit both continuous and intermittent signs, the intermittent sign should be used to indicate a higher level of danger or a more urgent need for the requested/imposed intervention or action than is indicated by the continuous sign.

The duration of each flash and the frequency of the flashers of an intermittent illuminated sign must be such as to

—

ensure the proper perception of the message, and

—

avoid any confusion either between different illuminated signs or with a continuous illuminated sign.

2.2.&nbsp;If a flashing sign is used instead of — or together with — an acoustic signal, identical codes must be used.

2.3.&nbsp;Devices for emitting flashing signs in the event of grave danger must be under special surveillance or be fitted with an auxiliary lamp.

<a id="anx_VII"></a>

<a id="id-078e491c-df78-4e4e-a473-440a0d37d734"></a>ANNEX VII

<a id="id-0164ed67-7bef-4a08-9012-c86bea5baaa6"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR ACOUSTIC SIGNS

<a id="id-e1f5721d-831c-47ad-aba2-be8d6bfcb37c"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intrinsic features

1.1.&nbsp;Acoustic signals must:

(a)

have a sound level which is considerably higher than the level of ambient noise, so that it is audible without being excessive or painful;

(b)

be easily recognizable, particularly in terms of pulse length and the interval between pulses or groups of pulses, and be clearly distinct from any other acoustic signal and ambient noises.

1.2.&nbsp;If a device can emit an acoustic signal at variable and constant frequencies, the variable frequency should be used to indicate a higher level of danger or a more urgent need for the requested/imposed intervention or action in relation to the stable frequency.

<a id="id-6cc06063-c680-4cdd-910f-e363db720db1"></a>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Code

The signal for evacuation must be continuous.

<a id="anx_VIII"></a>

<a id="id-8bcfe4db-2726-45c0-be3f-c77c0e1b04f3"></a>ANNEX VIII

<a id="id-a5b3bee1-7b36-4247-97bd-250c10b31c04"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR VERBAL COMMUNICATION

<a id="id-013be5cc-664d-4eae-8a10-3e023da6a719"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intrinsic features

1.1.&nbsp;Verbal communication between a speaker or emitter and one or more hearers is to take the form of (sometimes coded) short texts, phrases, groups of words and/or individual words.

1.2.&nbsp;Spoken messages are to be as short, simple and clear as possible; the verbal skills of the speaker and the hearing abilities of the hearer(s) must be such as to ensure reliable verbal communication.

1.3.&nbsp;Verbal communication is direct (by means of the human voice) or indirect (by means of a human or artificial voice which is broadcast by whatever means is appropriate).

<a id="id-72b2bd9a-e72e-4321-87fa-5387938ba70e"></a>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Specific rules governing use

2.1.&nbsp;The persons involved must have a good knowledge of the language used so that they are able to pronounce and understand the spoken message correctly and consequently behave in a way which is appropriate to health and/or safety.

2.2.&nbsp;If verbal communication is used instead of — or together with — gestures, code words should be used such as:

<a id="anx_I"></a>

<a id="id-40feadf8-7dae-4f9b-9755-4d068cf15851"></a>ANNEX IX

<a id="id-271ba4e8-8885-49dc-a793-fdd88abc4596"></a>MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS FOR HAND SIGNALS

<a id="id-c76f794e-f0e5-41ae-b1be-b5a63d962de0"></a>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Features

Hand signals must be precise, simple, expansive, easy to make and to understand, and clearly distinct from other such signals.

Where both arms are used at the same time, they must be moved symmetrically and for giving one sign only.

Provided that they fulfil the conditions given above, the signals used may vary slightly from or be more detailed than those shown in section 3; they must, however, be equally meaningful and comprehensible.

<a id="id-bd656196-58ef-404a-9974-632a6251748e"></a>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Specific rules governing use

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.1.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The person giving the signs, hereinafter referred to as the ‘signalman’, will use arm/hand movements to give manoeuvring instructions to the person receiving the signs, hereinafter referred to as the (operator).</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.2.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The signalman must be able to monitor all manoeuvres visually without being endangered thereby.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.3.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The signalman’s duties must consist exclusively of directing manoeuvres and ensuring the safety of workers in the vicinity.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.4.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">If the conditions described in point 2.2 are not fulfilled, one or more extra singnalmen should be deployed.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.5.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">The operator must interrupt the ongoing manoeuvre in order to request new instructions when he is unable to carry out the orders he has received with the necessary safety guarantees.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>

<table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<colgroup><col width="5%">
<col width="95%">
</colgroup><tbody><tr>
<td valign="top">
<p class="norm">2.6.</p>
</td>
<td valign="top">Accessories:<p class="norm">The operator must be able to recognize the signalman without difficulty.</p>
<p class="norm">The signalman is to wear one or more appropriate distinctive items, e.g. a jacket, helmet, sleeves or armbandds, or carry bats.</p>
<p class="norm">The distinctive items are to be brightly coloured, preferably all of the same colour and for the exclusive use of signalmen.</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>
